_comment: Figures that appear with their instrument in exactly one document, per DOCS-POLICY rule 2, and are cited rather than restated everywhere else. backend/tools/audit-docs.py check C4 reads this file and reports every match OUTSIDE the owner. A row is a name, the owning document, a regex, and an optional `allowed` list of fnmatch patterns where a copy is deliberate. Allowances are explicit rows, never a global ignore: 'we decided this copy is fine' is exactly the kind of decision that has to be written down where the next reader sees it. Matches inside fenced code blocks are skipped by the checker, so a shell transcript quoting a number is not a finding.
_why: The failure this prevents is already in the tree and is what motivated the rule. The main suite's test count is written as three different values in three live documents and none of them is what the runner prints; each was correct on the day it was typed. Nothing was wrong -- the number was copied to four places and only one of them was ever updated again. A general duplicate-number detector is not possible and must not be attempted, so this checks a DECLARED list. It will never be complete, and the declaration is as much the deliverable as the code is.
_scope_note: SEEDED WITH ONE ROW by task 36; the other seven added by task 38 (2026-08-01), which did the sweep. Task 36 deliberately invented no rows, because who owns what is the part of rule 2 a script cannot decide. Every row below states its owner, the measurement behind its pattern, and the reason for each allowance.
_allowance_rule: WHICH DOCUMENTS THIS CHECK BITES ON, and it is rule 1's lifecycle table rather than anyone's taste. `contract` and `rolling` may not be stale -- a stale contract is a defect and a rolling document is rewritten every session -- so those are where a copied figure is a real hazard and they are never allowed. `record`, `task` and `rationale` are FROZEN by construction: a record is history and says so, a task file freezes at its Status, and DOCS-POLICY's closing line is 'append-only means append-only'. Rewriting a figure in one of those destroys the only evidence the number was ever different, which is rule 4's whole argument and is what docs/archive/* was already allowed for. So the allowances below are frozen-kind documents, enumerated rather than globbed by kind because fnmatch cannot read frontmatter. They are enumerated to what each figure ACTUALLY REACHES today: a frozen document that starts quoting one of these later will fire once, and the fix is to add it here with a line saying why -- not to widen the rule.
_unit_note: THE UNIT OF A CLAIM IS THE SENTENCE, AND A STRUCK FIGURE IS NOT A RESTATEMENT. Both landed 2026-08-02 with task 46 and both are properties of the CHECKER, in `figure_hits()` -- stated once here rather than nine times below, which is this file's own rule applied to itself. (1) Every `^(?![^\n]*...)` lookahead below licenses a figure that names its metric or cites its owner, and it used to be scoped to the physical line. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is hard-wrapped at ~88 columns, so a compliant sentence put `94.8%` on one line and the `agree2` licensing it on the next: the prose satisfied rule 3's corollary exactly as written and the check could not see it. Task 38's design was right against the corpus it was measured on -- docs/, where no registered figure straddled a wrap -- and widening the scanned set to the two roots is what moved the population. The licence is now tested against the SENTENCE, deliberately not the paragraph: measured 2026-08-02, the sentence licenses 3 lines and the paragraph 7, and the extra 4 are licensed by a token belonging to a DIFFERENT claim that happens to be adjacent. (2) A figure inside a `~~struck~~` span is exempt, per occurrence and not per sentence, so a live figure beside a struck one still fires. Rule 4 mandates struck-and-kept and 235 struck spans across 48 documents under docs/ are doing it; reporting a number whose own sentence disowns it penalises the one behaviour the policy requires outright. THE MATCH ITSELF IS STILL LINE-SCOPED and only the licence widened, which makes the new finding set a strict SUBSET of the old one by construction. Task 46 assumed that property held of the regexes -- 'widening a match can only ever CLEAR findings, never add them' -- and it does not: the webapp, labelling-rate and labelled-36 rows are proximity patterns, and a naive paragraph re-scope of the nine INVENTS 2 matches while clearing 10. Both invented matches are real cross-wrap occurrences in files these rows already allow, so the line scope has false negatives of the same shape as its false positives; widening the match body is a real follow-up with its own measurement, and it is not this change.
_owner_note: docs/tasks/refactor/AUDIT.md owns the run-level figures because it was built for exactly that and its own header says it 'indexes; it does not restate'. It is NOT the owner of everything: the Pursuit gate volume is owned by docs/pursuit-gate-volume.md, which carries the SQL, the date range and the junk-fraction adjustment. Rule 2 puts a figure with its instrument, and the instrument for that one is not in AUDIT.md.

figures.name: main suite test count
figures._note: AUDIT.md owns it and, as of task 38, DOES NOT STATE IT: rule 3 says a number a script can produce is never typed into prose, so the table there carries the command and the instruction to read `Ran N tests`. An owner with no copy is the intended end state for this row, not an omission. The four-digit band is the figure's shape: every count this run has printed since 2026-07-29 -- 1107, 1160, 1166, 1171, 1178, 1182, 1233 -- lives there.
figures._pattern_note: THE BAND WAS WIDENED FROM `11[0-9]{2}` AND THE OLD ONE WAS ALREADY BROKEN. The seeded pattern was written when the suite printed 1182; it printed 1233 the next day, which `11[0-9]{2}` cannot see at all -- the row silently stopped checking the live number within a day of being written, which is the same decay it exists to catch. `1[0-9]{3}` covers 1000-1999 and needs three exclusions, each measured on 2026-08-01 over every .md under docs/: (1) the seeded lookarounds refusing ':' '.' '-' and adjacent digits, which is what keeps `ingest/ats.py:1128` and `labels.py:1112-1145` out -- a naive \b11[0-9]{2}\b matched 86 lines of which 34 were LINE-NUMBER CITATIONS, and the lookarounds dropped all 34 and kept all 52; (2) '=' added to the lookbehind, which drops `$limit=1000` in docs/ingest/nyc-open-data.md:83, the only false positive the widening introduced in a document this row bites on; (3) hex letters added to both lookarounds, which drops six matches inside sha256 digests and short commit hashes (`afb2d58f5d369dfd03ad9237a8b16396...`, `1074b7f0354bc3cceed49194`, `scratch_c1388ee2`). What remains is 69 lines over 7 files, of which exactly 3 are not test counts -- `1630` and `1285` in a source-volume table and `1099` as in the tax form -- and all 3 sit in frozen records that are allowed anyway. A check that cries wolf is worse than no check, because it teaches the reflex that retires all the others. RE-RECORDED 2026-08-02 BY TASK 46, against the sentence-scoped licence and the strikethrough exemption of `_unit_note`, over the CURRENT scanned set (docs/ plus the two roots). The 2026-08-01 counts above are superseded twice over -- they are line-scoped AND docs/-only -- and are kept because they are the measurement the pattern was SHAPED by, which the new counts do not replace. This row: 81 lines in 16 files line-scoped, 74 lines in 14 files now. All 7 cleared are STRUCK, none is a sentence effect, and every one is struck-and-kept history a reader is meant to see -- ~~1107~~, ~~1070~~, ~~1166~~, ~~1171~~ in docs/archive/handoff-state-2026-07-31.md:31,56,95,96, a ~~1166~~ inside a strike spanning three lines in docs/archive/handoff-tree-state.md:30-32, the `~~1182~~` this task's own file quotes at tranche_seven/46-sentence-scope-the-c4-lookahead.md:25, and `.claude/CLAUDE.md:196`. Six of the seven sit in files this row already allows, so the only one that was a FINDING is the last. THIS ROW IS THE REASON TASK 46 NEEDED A SECOND FIX: it is the one row of the nine with NO compliance lookahead, so no re-scoping of the licence could ever have cleared it -- joining the paragraph still matches `1182`. Task 46's premise that both C4 findings had one cause was wrong here, and only here.
figures._allowed_note: All six are frozen kinds; see _allowance_rule. The two judgement calls task 36 explicitly deferred to task 38 are settled here. CLAUDE_UPDATES.md is ALLOWED: it is `kind: record`, its per-commit counts are the evidence that the suite grew, and rewriting them would be the same destruction of history that docs/archive/* is allowed to prevent. tranche_seven/38-one-figure-one-owner.md is allowed by the `tranche_*` glob, but its copies were REMOVED rather than relied on -- the file arguing that a typed count decays should not be quoting three of them. NOT allowed, deliberately: docs/tasks/refactor/HANDOFF.md, which is the only `kind: rolling` document in the tree and therefore the one place rule 1 forbids a stale figure outright. It is the live entry point every session reads. Its findings are in doc-policy-baseline.json and are task 40's to clear. ADDED 2026-08-01, by the procedure this file prescribes rather than by widening the rule: DECISIONS.md is `kind: rationale` -- append-only and frozen -- and DEC-71 quotes all three conflicting values (1182, 1178, 1160) because naming them IS the entry. An entry recording that a figure drifted cannot cite the owner instead of the drift. This is the same argument CLAUDE_UPDATES.md is allowed under, and C4 fired on the entry while it was being written, which is the third time it has caught the orchestrator restating an owned figure in one session. ~~HANDOFF.md ADDED 2026-08-01 by the orchestrator, REVERSING task 38's decision to allow it nowhere, and the reversal is on evidence task 38 did not have.~~ REMOVED 2026-08-01 BY TASK 44, WHICH LANDED. Struck and kept per rule 4, because the reasoning below is what the row was decided on and is the record of a temporary hole; the paragraph read: Task 38 believed the file held one or two restatements and argued -- correctly, on that belief -- that the only kind: rolling document in the tree is the worst possible exemption. It holds NINETEEN, and every one of them sits below line 380: none is in the START HERE block or in the three standing READ THIS FIRST sections, which were cleaned in 40a and :383 and stay clean. They are struck-and-kept sequences -- ~~1107~~ ~~1160~~ ~~1166~~ ~~1171~~ 1178 -- that ARE the record of the drift this tranche exists to document, and rewriting them would destroy the evidence under rule 4 exactly as it would in CLAUDE_UPDATES.md. THE REAL FINDING IS THAT THIS FILE IS TWO DOCUMENTS: a rolling entry point on top of a frozen session narrative, and rule 1 has no name for that. C4 cannot see the boundary because fnmatch is per-file. Task 44 is opened to archive the history region, which removes this allowance rather than widening it. Until then this row is blind to HANDOFF.md and that is a known hole, not a clean result. TASK 44 LANDED 2026-08-01 AND THE HOLE IS CLOSED: the frozen narrative is at docs/archive/handoff-state-2026-07-31.md and docs/archive/handoff-tree-state.md, and this row now enforces on HANDOFF.md like every other contract. ONE PREMISE OF TASK 44 WAS WRONG AND IS WORTH THE NEXT READER'S TIME: it assumed all nineteen sat in the history region, so that a red C4 after the move would mean 'something that should have been archived was not'. Seventeen did. The other two -- a `suite 1030 -> 1058` delta in the next-steps list and a `Suite 1171 -> 1178` delta in an open follow-up -- sat inside LIVE rolling sections, where archiving them would have archived current content. Both became citations of a document that already carried the pair (docs/archive/handoff-gate-fix.md and CLAUDE_UPDATES.md), which is rule 2's fix rather than rule 4's, and nothing was lost. The general form: a figure inside a rolling document is not evidence that the surrounding section is history.
